payload.task_text:
Academic affairs wants to conduct a grade equity review to see whether grading standards have remained consistent across consecutive fall semesters. We need to look at courses that were offered in both Fall 2013 and Fall 2014 and compare how students performed in each offering. There is a grading standards PDF in your workspace called Grading_Standards.pdf that defines the grade bands and equity thresholds we use, along with a guide.md that explains the methodology.

Pull course listings and student grade data from the learning management system. Focus on fall semester offerings from 2013 and 2014. For each course that appears in both years, compute the average student score and pass rate for each year. A student's score should be their average across all assignment submissions in that course. Only include students who have at least one scored submission in the course offering; students with no submissions are excluded from that course's statistics.

Create an Excel file called Grade_Equity_Analysis.xlsx with three sheets. All numeric values in the file must be written as literal numbers (do not use Excel formulas). The first sheet should be called Course Comparison and should have columns Course_Name (the base course name without the semester, sorted alphabetically), Fall_2013_Mean (rounded to 1 decimal), Fall_2014_Mean (rounded to 1 decimal), Score_Difference (the 2014 mean minus the 2013 mean, rounded to 1 decimal), Fall_2013_Pass_Rate (rounded to 1 decimal), Fall_2014_Pass_Rate (rounded to 1 decimal), Pass_Rate_Change (rounded to 1 decimal), and Equity_Status. The equity status should be Acceptable if the absolute score difference is less than 5, Concerning if between 5 and 10 inclusive, or Action Required if greater than 10. Only include courses that have data in both fall semesters.

The second sheet should be called Grade Distribution and should have columns Course_Name, Year, A_Count, B_Count, C_Count, D_Count, F_Count, and Total_Students. There should be two rows per course, one for 2013 and one for 2014. Use the grade bands from the standards document to classify students.

The third sheet should be called Summary with columns Metric and Value. Include rows for Total_Courses_Compared, Courses_Acceptable, Courses_Concerning, Courses_Action_Required, Overall_Avg_2013 (rounded to 1 decimal), Overall_Avg_2014 (rounded to 1 decimal), and Overall_Change (rounded to 1 decimal). Overall_Avg_2013 is the mean of every included student's mean score across all six compared courses in Fall 2013 (sum of all per-student means divided by the total number of students in those courses), and Overall_Avg_2014 is the same for Fall 2014. Overall_Change = Overall_Avg_2014 minus Overall_Avg_2013.

Write a Word document called Equity_Report.docx with sections for Executive Summary, Methodology, Course-by-Course Analysis, Recommendations, and Appendix. The executive summary should highlight key findings. The course-by-course section should discuss each compared course. The recommendations section should call out any courses requiring faculty review.

For each course that has an Action Required equity status, schedule a 45-minute faculty review meeting on Google Calendar during the week of March 16 to 20, 2026. Title each meeting with the course name followed by Grade Equity Review and include the equity details in the description.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, use one parallel owner per matched course family; do not split a course into page agents and do not add an aggregation agent. Canvas is read-only. Resolve the runtime workspace dynamically and give each owner one runtime-unique JSON path.

The main agent first reads Grading_Standards.pdf and guide.md completely, freezes the literal grade bands, pass threshold, per-student averaging rule and equity boundaries, and calls canvas_list_courses(include_ended=true) once. Verify the six matched base names and the exact offering pairs AAA 1/2, BBB 3/4, DDD 9/10, EEE 13/14, FFF 16/17, and GGG 20/21, retaining each offering's exact full Canvas name.

Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 6 explore sub-agents in parallel, one per literal pair below:

   1. explore 0 (enterprise-data-analyst 0): Pair owner for AAA offerings course_id=1 and course_id=2. Request the two offerings' page 1 together in one native-parallel response with canvas_list_student_submissions(course_id=<id>, student_ids=["all"], grouped=false, page=1, per_page=100), then issue both offerings' remaining literal pages revealed by total_pages together in native-parallel batches and verify every page identity. Use literal row.id as submission identity, retain only rows with a numeric score, group them by user_id, compute each included student's mean over all scored submissions, and exclude students with none. Write one compact JSON containing the two complete per-student mean arrays, grade-band counts, student counts, score sums, page identities, submission IDs/counts and duplicate controls; read it back; and return only path/hash and those controls. Do not return raw submissions in chat or use final_score/current_score in place of submission.score.
   2. explore 1 (enterprise-data-analyst 1): Pair owner for BBB offerings course_id=3 and course_id=4 — same literal recipe, only the two offering identities and unique output path substituted.
   3. explore 2 (enterprise-data-analyst 2): Pair owner for DDD offerings course_id=9 and course_id=10 — same literal recipe, only the two offering identities and unique output path substituted.
   4. explore 3 (enterprise-data-analyst 3): Pair owner for EEE offerings course_id=13 and course_id=14 — same literal recipe, only the two offering identities and unique output path substituted.
   5. explore 4 (enterprise-data-analyst 4): Pair owner for FFF offerings course_id=16 and course_id=17 — same literal recipe, only the two offering identities and unique output path substituted.
   6. explore 5 (enterprise-data-analyst 5): Pair owner for GGG offerings course_id=20 and course_id=21 — same literal recipe, only the two offering identities and unique output path substituted.

After Wave 1, the main agent requires all six pair receipts and every advertised page exactly once. It computes the two means and pass rates per family, Score_Difference=2014-2013, Pass_Rate_Change likewise, and Equity_Status from raw differences: Acceptable for abs(diff)<5, Concerning for 5<=abs(diff)<=10, Action Required for abs(diff)>10. Overall_Avg_2013 and Overall_Avg_2014 are pooled over all included per-student means, not means of course means. Round only stored output values to one decimal and freeze one canonical packet with six comparison rows, twelve distribution rows and seven Summary metrics.

Then dispatch the three independent final branches in one native-parallel response:

- coder 0 (office-report-builder 0): Sole-write Grade_Equity_Analysis.xlsx with exactly Course Comparison, Grade Distribution and Summary, the task's literal headers, six alphabetically sorted family rows, two distribution rows per family, literal numeric values, and no formulas. Read every populated range back and recompute pass-rate denominators and summary counts from the returned cells.
- coder 1 (office-report-builder 1): Sole-write Equity_Report.docx with explicit Executive Summary, Methodology, Course-by-Course Analysis, Recommendations and Appendix headings, discussion of all six families, and every Action Required review. Read document text/structure back.
- coder 2 (external-workflow-operator 0): For only Action Required rows, sort by full course name and assign consecutive non-overlapping 45-minute slots during March 16-20, 2026. Search existing events by exact summary/start/end first; create each missing event at most once with summary <Course_Name> Grade Equity Review and its score/pass-rate changes in the description; then get_event for every retained ID. Use a timezone only if a visible task/calendar setting supplies it, otherwise omit the override.

Do not dispatch page, aggregation or audit agents after the output wave. Final acceptance requires the externally read workbook, document and calendar events to match the source-backed canonical packet; an early failed read is not completion.
